hook: Block a scene from above, then sit in any seat in the house: see who is hidden behind whom, who is upstaging whom and where the eye goes, and let the director's notes check your blocking from all sixteen seats.
outcome: Place actors, set pieces and lights for a scripted scene, read it from any seat in the house, and revise the blocking until the director's notes are met
sources: NCAS Theatre TH:Cr1, TH:Pr5, TH:Cr3: https://www.nationalartsstandards.org/

Alexander Dean and Lawrence Carra, Fundamentals of Play Directing, 5th ed. (Waveland Press, 1989): stage areas from the actor's point of view, the five body positions, upstaging, emphasis by position, level, light and movement
Settings, not facts: stage, set and seat sizes, sightline thresholds and focus weights are this tool's own, shown as a rough guide
Scenes: original, written for this tool
Stage, seat view, figures and set drawn in code
